extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners (agents/attorneys), disciplinary counsel, and parties in USPTO OED disciplinary proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and criteria used in USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline (OED) proceedings to determine misconduct, entry of default, cooperation obligations, and sanctions (including exclusion from practice). Applies statutory/regulatory duties under 37 C.F.R. and the process for imposing discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default/admission for failure to answer
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to file a timely answer to the Complaint constitutes an admission of the allegations and 'may result in entry of default judgment.' (37 C.F.R. § 11.36(e)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If properly served and no answer is filed within the time prescribed, the respondent is deemed to have admitted the factual allegations and the OED Director may move for default judgment; the court may grant the Default Motion and issue an Initial Decision on Default Judgment. (Procedural authority to hear and issue decision cited at 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19 and 11.39.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty: refrain from disreputable or gross misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not engage in disreputable or gross misconduct. (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This broad prohibition supports findings of professional misconduct where a practitioner's conduct abuses their status or otherwise undermines professional standards (illustrated by the respondent's multiple offenses).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty: no dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not engage in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation. (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4); 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: representing oneself to be authorized to practice law in a state when not authorized. Such misrepresentations support disciplinary violations under these provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty: do not engage in conduct prejudicial to administration of justice
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not engage in conduct that is prejudicial to the administration of justice. (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Representations or actions that impair the functioning of courts or fairness of proceedings (e.g., falsely holding out authority to represent a client leading to dismissal or bench warrant) fall within this prohibition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty: avoid other conduct reflecting adversely on fitness to practice
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not engage in any other conduct that adversely reflects on the practitioner's fitness to practice before the Office. (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6); 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule is available for additional unspecified misconduct; the court will only find a violation under this clause if 'other conduct' of the requisite nature is alleged and supported by the record. (In this case the OED Director had not alleged additional 'other conduct'.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on holding out as an attorney when not one
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless a practitioner is an attorney, the practitioner shall not hold himself or herself out to be an attorney or lawyer. (37 C.F.R. § 10.31(d)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Falsely identifying oneself as an attorney or 'federal attorney' or using USPTO registration as a substitute for state bar licensure violates this provision; the decision cites multiple instances where the respondent identified himself as an attorney despite not being licensed in Colorado.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty: not to prejudice or damage a client
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not intentionally prejudice or damage a client during the course of a professional relationship. (37 C.F.R. § 10.84(a)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct such as failing to prepare/file a client's patent application, abandoning the client, and failing to refund advance payments constitutes violating this duty (here, failure to perform services and to return $1,820).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty when appearing before a tribunal: do not intentionally or habitually violate disciplinary rules
rubrics_metrics.description: When appearing in a professional capacity before a tribunal, a practitioner shall not intentionally or habitually violate the USPTO Disciplinary Rules. (37 C.F.R. § 10.89(c)(6)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appearing in court after being informed one is not authorized to do so, or repeatedly asserting unauthorized credentials before tribunals, supports violation of this rule (the respondent appeared and was told he could not represent the client, yet continued related filings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of reasonable diligence and promptness
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall act with reasonable diligence and promptness in representing a client. (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(a) via § 11.103).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to prepare, file, or prosecute a client's application and failure to respond to client communications constitute breaches of this duty (examples: respondent did not prepare or file Mr. Lyke's application and did not respond to repeated inquiries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to keep client reasonably informed
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall keep the client reasonably informed about the status of the matter. (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(a) via § 11.104(a)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not responding to a client's numerous attempts to communicate and abandoning the client are violations; the decision cites multiple missed responses to the client's inquiries as supporting this finding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to promptly comply with reasonable client requests for information
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall promptly comply with reasonable requests for information from the client. (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(a) via § 11.104(a)(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeated failure to respond to client's requests for information (e.g., status inquiries) constitutes a violation under this provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty regarding client funds and accounting
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall promptly deliver to the client any funds that the client is entitled to receive and, upon request by the client, shall promptly render a full accounting regarding such property. (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(a) via § 11.115(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepting advance fees and failing to refund them when services were not performed (here, $1,820) violates this provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to cooperate with OED and not fail to correct misapprehensions
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not fail to disclose a fact necessary to correct a misapprehension known by the person to have arisen in the matter, fail to cooperate with the OED in an investigation of any matter before it, or knowingly fail to respond to a lawful demand or request for information from an admissions or disciplinary authority. (37 C.F.R. § 11.801(b) via § 11.804(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to respond to OED Requests for Information (RFIs), certified letters, and other investigation communications supports a violation; USPS certified-mail receipts documenting delivery but no response are cited as evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors for determining sanctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Before sanctioning a practitioner, the Court must consider: (1) whether the practitioner violated a duty owed to a client, the public, the legal system, or the profession; (2) whether the practitioner acted intentionally, knowingly, or negligently; (3) the amount of the actual or potential injury caused by the practitioner's misconduct; and (4) the existence of any aggravating or mitigating factors. (37 C.F.R. § 11.54(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision applies these four factors: finds violation of duties to client and profession; finds knowing/intentional conduct (based on accepting fees, misrepresentations, ignoring courts and RFIs); documents actual/potential injury (lost fees, jeopardized IP, dismissal of civil claim, bench warrant); and finds aggravating factors (multiple offenses, ignoring investigation and communications). The court uses ABA Standards for Imposing Lawyer Sanctions as guidance in assessing aggravation/mitigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to exclude from practice and scope of sanction
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director may request exclusion from practice before the USPTO in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters; the court may impose exclusion when misconduct and the sanction factors warrant it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where violations are knowing, cause substantial actual/potential harm, and aggravating factors exist, the court may order exclusion (maximum sanction). The decision here grants exclusion based on the findings and analysis under § 11.54(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal requirements and timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal from the Initial Decision must be filed with the USPTO within 30 days after the date of the Initial Decision and must include exceptions to the ALJ's Decision and supporting reasons. (37 C.F.R. § 11.55; filing address per 37 C.F.R. § 1.1(a)(3)(ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to file a timely appeal in accordance with the regulation is deemed acceptance of the Initial Decision and waiver of administrative and judicial review rights.
